Issue Number: close #41622 close #42003

Problem Summary:

### What is changed and how it works?

Build plan need to use the same InfoSchema, but `vars.InTxn()` is false in #41622.
Relax the condition can fix issue/41622

Alternative: change all `sctx.GetInfoSchema()` to `sessiontxn.GetTxnManager(sctx).GetTxnInfoSchema()`
It involves a lot of changes and seems more fragile comparing to this single line of change.

issue_context.title: query `information_schema.tables` will report table not exists
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

1. create a table that contains an auto_increament column and then drop the table
2. run query `SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.tables`

parallel run these two steps several times, you may get an error `Table xxx doesn't exist`

this is because https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/5ff5b346912924d10af609d081933aaad46536ae/executor/infoschema_reader.go#L687-L692 
`getAutoIncrementID` will use the newest schema that the table has been dropped.
sleep seconds at L687 will easier to reproduce this bug

similar with https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/41622

<!-- a step by step guide for reproducing the bug. -->

review_comments:
I don't know why this work? 
I thought we should use `sessiontxn.GetTxnManager(p.sctx).GetTxnInfoSchema()` instead of `GetInfoSchema` since `GetInfoSchema` was been marked as deprecated.

`vars.InTxn()` is not set when building plan, and the infoschema may change during building (and also during executing)
`vars.TxnCtx.InfoSchema` is set anyway, so relax the `vars.InTxn()` check here can make the building process use the correct infoschema, i.e. `vars.TxnCtx.InfoSchema`

`GetInfoSchema()` spread all over the code base, involves much more change.
